bootstrap.notes: Read ml/00-problem-framing/handoff.json directly (same session, same repo).

decisions.decision: Spine = social_post rows where platform in ('facebook', 'instagram'), one row per post, grain confirmed at 360 rows (228 facebook + 132 instagram) before any join.
decisions.rationale: Matches 00-problem-framing's scope decision to exclude Threads from the primary label. Grain is the natural one for this problem: one prediction per post.

decisions.decision: Joined social_post to social_metrics_snapshot on social_post_id, taking it as one row per post rather than assuming a single snapshot exists structurally.
decisions.rationale: The schema's own UNIQUE constraint is (social_post_id, captured_at), not social_post_id alone — meaning multiple snapshots per post over time are structurally allowed even though the current data happens to have exactly one per post. Checked empirically rather than trusting a same-named column pattern; today there is no fan-out, but a future re-ingest with periodic re-snapshots would need this query changed to pick the latest captured_at.

decisions.decision: Facebook's 10 posts with content_type = NULL will be recoded to a literal 'unknown' category at feature-prep time, not dropped and not imputed to an existing class.
decisions.rationale: This is a deterministic recode of a raw categorical (upstream data-entry gap, not a value to be learned), so it belongs here per the 01/03 split rule, not in the model pipeline as a learned imputation.

decisions.decision: Add a derived boolean feature `is_video` (true when content_type in {'video','reel'}) alongside the raw per-platform content_type, to be computed in stage 03's feature step.
decisions.rationale: The two primary platforms use different vocabulary for the same medium: Facebook posts are labeled 'video', Instagram's equivalent is labeled 'reel' (Instagram's content_type CHECK constraint doesn't even include 'video' as an allowed value). Feeding raw content_type alone would force the model to re-learn that 'video'≈'reel' from ~360 rows; a deterministic derived flag encodes the known fact directly.

decisions.decision: No imputation performed in this stage. content_type nulls are recoded to a named category (a deterministic label, not a guessed value); no other column has missing values requiring imputation.
decisions.rationale: Per the kernel rule: imputation parameters are learned from data and belong in the stage 03 pipeline, fit on training folds only.

assertions.claim: Spine row count (facebook + instagram social_post rows) was counted independently before any join.
assertions.method: SELECT platform, count(*) FROM social_post WHERE platform IN ('facebook','instagram') GROUP BY 1

assertions.claim: The join key between social_post and social_metrics_snapshot was verified against the actual FK/constraint catalog, not assumed from column naming.
assertions.method: Queried pg_constraint directly for both tables.
assertions.evidence: fk_social_metrics_snapshot_social_post_id: FOREIGN KEY (social_post_id) REFERENCES social_post(id) ON DELETE CASCADE. uq_social_metrics_snapshot_post_captured_at: UNIQUE (social_post_id, captured_at) -- composite, not social_post_id alone.

assertions.claim: Checked empirically (not just via the declared constraint) whether any post currently has more than one metrics snapshot.
assertions.method: SELECT social_post_id, count(*) FROM social_metrics_snapshot GROUP BY 1 HAVING count(*) > 1
assertions.evidence: Zero posts with more than one snapshot today (0 rows returned), despite the schema structurally allowing it. Recorded as decision join-latest-snapshot-not-assume-single since this could change.

assertions.claim: No orphaned social_post rows (posts with zero snapshots) among the two primary platforms, and the join preserved the spine's row count.
assertions.method: Anti-join count (posts with no matching snapshot) plus a direct INNER JOIN row count compared against the independently-counted spine.
assertions.evidence: 0 posts with zero snapshots (checked across all platforms, not just the two primary ones). Joined count = 360, exactly matching the spine count of 360 -- no fan-out, no silent row loss.

assertions.claim: Every candidate feature (platform, content_type, caption, posted_at-derived day-of-week/hour) exists at prediction_time (immediately before publishing); no post-hoc metric was included as a feature.
assertions.method: Manual review of the candidate feature list against problem_spec.prediction_time and the table schema. impressions/reach/likes/comments/shares/saves/clicks all live only in social_metrics_snapshot, which is populated after a post goes live -- confirmed excluded from features, used only to construct the label.

assertions.claim: The expanding per-platform median label (defined in 00-problem-framing) was actually computed on the real Facebook+Instagram data, and its class balance measured, before any split design.
assertions.method: SQL window-function computation of the expanding median per platform (posts ordered by posted_at), applied to compute the binary label, then counted per platform and combined.
assertions.evidence: facebook: 97/228 positive (42.5%); instagram: 70/132 positive (53.0%); combined: 167/360 positive (46.4%). Non-degenerate -- confirms the 00-problem-framing scoping decision (excluding Threads) produced a usable label on the platforms that remain.

assertions.claim: Searched explicitly for sentinel codes and impossible values (not just relying on NOT NULL/CHECK constraints already enforced by the schema).
assertions.method: Reviewed the CHECK constraints (ck_social_metrics_snapshot_nonneg enforces all engagement metrics >= 0 at the database level) and manually inspected caption length distribution and content_type value sets for anything that looked like a disguised sentinel (e.g. a suspicious repeated exact value).
assertions.evidence: No sentinel codes found. content_type NULL (10 Facebook rows) is genuine missingness, not a disguised sentinel -- handled via decision recode-null-content-type. No impossible values (all engagement/impression/reach counts are schema-enforced non-negative; posted_at values fall within a real 2026-04-26 to 2026-09-22 range, no future timestamps).

risks.description: 228 (Facebook) and 132 (Instagram) posts respectively -- enough for a first classical baseline but not for a per-platform model; the initial model will need to pool both platforms with `platform` as a feature rather than training two separate models.
risks.mitigation: Already reflected in problem_spec's stopping condition; 03-modeling should try a pooled model first and treat separate per-platform models as a stretch goal, not the default.

risks.description: Facebook and Instagram use different content_type vocabularies for the same underlying medium (video vs. reel), and Instagram's CHECK constraint doesn't even permit 'video' as a value.
risks.mitigation: Addressed via decision derive-is-video-cross-platform; raw content_type is kept as a feature too since 'reel' vs 'carousel' vs 'image' still carries platform-specific signal beyond just video/not-video.

risks.description: Caption text (21-1446 chars on Facebook, 23-993 on Instagram) is a real free-text field with no decided feature representation yet -- raw text, derived stats (length/hashtag/emoji count), or a pretrained embedding per 00-problem-framing's transfer-learning decision.
risks.mitigation: Left to 03-modeling: start with cheap derived stats as the safe baseline feature set, evaluate whether a frozen pretrained embedding earns its added complexity only after that baseline exists.

risks.description: social_post.campaign_variant_id is NULL for all 360 rows in the primary-platform spine.
risks.mitigation: Expected -- this column links to paid-campaign attribution, and no paid campaign exists yet per DATA_CONSTRAINTS.md. Excluded from the feature set entirely rather than treated as a missing-value problem.

risks.description: Today every post has exactly one metrics snapshot, but the schema's UNIQUE constraint permits multiple snapshots per post over time (e.g. if re-ingestion starts capturing periodic snapshots rather than one-shot).
risks.mitigation: The extract query in ml/01-data/extract.py currently does a plain INNER JOIN, which is only correct because there is no fan-out today. If periodic snapshots are ever introduced, this query must be changed to select the latest captured_at per post before re-running any downstream stage.

outputs.name: Cached dataset extract
outputs.description: 360 rows (facebook+instagram social_post joined to its metrics snapshot), with the expanding per-platform median engagement and the resulting binary label already computed. Reproducible via ml/01-data/extract.py against the live warehouse.

outputs.name: Extraction script
outputs.description: Deterministic SQL extract + label computation. No learned parameters. Re-run anytime to regenerate the CSV.

next_stage_needs: 02-split: dataset.csv has 360 rows spanning 2026-04-26 to 2026-09-22 with posted_at as the natural time column -- consider whether a temporal split (train on earlier posts, test on later ones) better matches how this model would actually be used (predicting a not-yet-posted post) than a random split, even though problem_spec doesn't mandate one.

03-modeling: content_type has 10 NULLs on Facebook (recode to 'unknown' per decision recode-null-content-type) and a cross-platform vocabulary mismatch (see modality_screen and risks) -- derive is_video before one-hot encoding raw content_type.

03-modeling: caption representation is not yet decided -- start with derived stats (length, hashtag count) as the cheap baseline feature; a pretrained embedding feature is a later addition per 00-problem-framing's transfer-learning decision, not a default.

modality_screen.rationale: Predominantly tabular (platform, content_type, posted_at-derived day/hour) plus one free-text field (caption). Listed honestly as multimodal rather than pretending it's purely tabular, per the kernel's own warning against that specific failure mode. Route is still classical_first, not deep_learning_likely, for a stated reason: with only 360 rows, training any text/vision model from scratch is data-starved, and the caption field's realistic treatment -- per 00-problem-framing's transfer-learning decision -- is a FROZEN pretrained embedding used as an input feature to a classical model, not end-to-end deep learning. pretrained_models_available=true reflects that a pretrained sentence-embedding model exists and could supply that feature later; it does not mean this project trains a deep model. The deep-learning gate in 03-modeling has final say regardless of this route.
